correctness.rationale: Admissibility can only decrease. At a stopping time just after an acceptance, the currently admissible clocks have fresh independent unit exponential residual lives, so the minimum has rate equal to their number and is independent of the next chosen face. Independent exact replay derived the faces from the regular icosahedron coordinates and enumerated all successful histories by intersecting the remaining face sets in the conflict graph. It gave reachable-state counts 1,20,100,80,1 and exactly 10 six-site and 60 nine-site terminals each with weight 1/100, plus the full set with weight 3/10. Backtracking adjacency-preserving vertex maps gave the 120 automorphisms and the single orbit of each size; the vacancy checks on every mask confirmed the connected induced six-cycle or distances 1,2,3. Coverage is (6/12)(1/10)+(9/12)(3/5)+3/10=4/5. The entire rate-vector distribution is supported on (20,10), (20,10,4), (20,10,2), (20,10,4,1) with weights 1/10,3/10,3/10,3/10. Conditional transforms multiply the rate/(rate+s) factors, and the mixture yields both the stated transform for all s≥0 and exact mean 3/4 and variance 251/400. There is no waiting-time contribution from rejected proposals after jamming.
residual_risks: The clock and time laws require equal rate-one attempts; the object being counted is the terminal union of accepted sites, not the face tiling or proposal histories.

value.rationale: This is a natural finite benchmark for irreversible packing on a regular triangulated sphere. The full per-pattern distribution and exact kinetic law answer distinct questions: the former reveals that all imperfect terminal site sets have the same mass despite two sizes, and the latter quantifies the time cost of reaching any jammed outcome. A researcher can use the exact distribution and moments to check finite RSA or random-greedy computations without interpreting this as an asymptotic theorem.
residual_risks: Substrate-specific; no inference to extended lattices, other trimer shapes, or unequal event rates.
